newsitem.title: USA: Six Pacific Gas/Elec hydro plants damaged.
newsitem.headline: Six Pacific Gas/Elec hydro plants damaged.

text.p: A half dozen power plants associated with Pacific Gas and Electric Co's California hydroelectric dams were damaged during recent flooding, a company spokesman said Monday.
Of the utility's 71 hydroelectric projects, others have had problems with silt and feeder canals, said PG&E spokesman Bill Sessa, adding that the dams themselves were not damaged.
"It will be a couple of weeks before we get an exact assessment. Some projects we can't even get to," he added.
PG&E's hydroelectric plant's have a capacity of 3,900 megawatts, while annual output averages 13,000 gigawatt hours, Sessa said.
Information on hydroelectric output was not available.
Aside from the flood-related damage, the hydroelectric outlook is affected by overall precipitation and the rate of snowmelt.

The warm rain which caused the heavy flooding in California melted much of the lower elevation snowpack in the Sierra Nevada mountains, according to the National Weather Service station in Sacramento.
